title: Made a game where on Twitch, you vote where the story goes.
author: Philipp
selftext: Happy to talk about the tech stack, the conceptual challenges and so on! Also happy to see you playing it live, the game's at [https://twitch.tv/evertrail](https://twitch.tv/evertrail) This uses a lot of OpenAI APIs, from ChatGPT to Dall-E, and even the host is AI. The music reacts to the mood of the story. And every image is freshly made based on the voting. Cheers!

comments.author: Philipp
comments.body: Forgot to mention: You can also add custom story twists and items every few rounds when you win the +. This lets you introduce anything at all into the world.

comments.author: silencer47
comments.body: So everything is created on the fly? The story, the images?

replies.author: Philipp
replies.body: Yep, exactly! Only each world's first image and paragraph, to get things going, are created manually. You can switch between different worlds in this game, and also replace the hosts. For instance, some hosts are more educative, others more humorous, some hosts are acting as if they were party NPCs and so on...

replies.author: silencer47
replies.body: Very interesting! Do you feed it reference texts to shape and bound the story so it doesn't become too generic as AI is prone too? Or perhaps you give it detailed instructions?

replies.author: Philipp
replies.body:
Exactly! I have two core approaches:

1. The start station of the story sets the tone and influences a lot how it continues. I wrote the first paragraph, and a non-visible short backstory, and the first few choices.

2. In my database, for every world I have guardrails and guidelines that briefly tell the AI where the story is set, what time, what it should focus on. This won't determine the plot, but just things like "Medieval fantasy, with a touch of humor" or "Isometric city builder" (yes, there's even strategy gamer!). These text descriptions are then fed into every new prompt sent to OpenAI.

A lot of the conceptual work during testing with players was how to make the story advance at proper good speed. Without guidelines, ChatGPT has the tendency to endlessly dwell on safety! Imagine, in the beginning we had a sci-fi story where people wanted to teleport to another planet through a giant portal -- but ChatGPT kept pushing choices of first setting up security committees to discuss! So I had to tune the guardrails to really keep things exciting and moving... and for ChatGPT to not be scared of (fictional) risks & thrills!

replies.author: silencer47
replies.body: Definitely checking it out when I get home! Might want to ask you some more questions then.

replies.author: Philipp
replies.body: Great, cheers!

comments.author: DisasterNarrow4949

replies.author: Philipp
replies.body: Cheers! It's running right now, here: [https://twitch.tv/evertrail](https://twitch.tv/evertrail) Just vote with 1, 2 or 3. Every few rounds you can win a "+", then you can add your own twists or items or people to the story by typing +something something.

replies.author: DisasterNarrow4949
replies.body: Got it! Is there a way I can “host” my own game on my twitch channel or right now we are limited to play the game on the evertail channel?

replies.author: Philipp
replies.body:
Good question! We have full rehosting features, where people in your own channel can "merge" with the channels which my AI checks, and then voting happens together and you as host can take over and comment. You can then also disable the AI host so people can hear you instead. [Here's a video stream](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kUF166WtJ_A) of where a Twitcher named Sylvii played it.

While this feature is implemented, it's not actively usable without some preparations and mod rights giving and such (as the main AI is still only running one core channel, so not everyone can rehost it at the same time). If you have a bigger Twitch channel and want to give it a try, we can chat about it tho.

comments.author: E_den
comments.body:
How do you maintain a good quality/pace in this kind of generated story ?
 Do you just give up on that to bet on the quantity of options, are players staying engaged or is it a lot of newcomers pushing it "forward" ?
Does the story go "forward" (you already implemented an ending and several big key events.in the story) or is nothing pre-determined ?

replies.author: Philipp
replies.body:
Pacing is indeed a crucial challenge!

There are textual guardrails and instructions for every world (theme) available. They include such commands as "Move the story forward and make it exciting" and such. This is also to counter ChatGPT's urge to make everything safe & peaceful... understandable in real-world contexts, but not useful for fiction!

I would hope that players stay engaged when small groups are forming. Because then half the fun is chatting about the (sometimes ridiculous and funny) story, and figuring out ways together to move it on.

When there's not many people on, things become a bit more challenging. We were considering expanding the format with realtime-generated videos, but that tech is a bit slow and expensive still at the moment. Let's see what the future brings!

As for endings, most stories are never-ending (and they're never predetermined), but a bunch have special syntax and instructions to allow ChatGPT to kill to end the story. It's surprisingly difficult to convince the API to do that! One thing that would be possible are times hero's arcs, which would mean special instructions could trigger at certain times in the story...

replies.author: E_den
replies.body:
I gave it a try a little bit

Im not a fan of the current quality of AI generated content so Im probably not your target audience but it did not feel very engaging, the story feels vague (maybe shallow ?) for no reason, I spent longer waiting to go to the next choices than reading my current one. It might just not be for me or the quality/pacing might not be on point

Also a quick recap options in chat could be useful for people joining mid-story

A post mortem on this either when the projects end or after some time could be interesting though, I'd like to understand better why It felt off for me

replies.author: Philipp
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback!

Note that there's different worlds you can switch to, by typing !worlds
They sometimes have different pacing and dynamics.

But yes, I understand it could still be improved. For instance, there's not enough details, consistency and specifics in some images. We could switch to the new ChatGPT image generator but it's too slow. And as you noticed, even the current generation waiting time can be a bit long...

I think it's more fun in a group... because then it's almost like playing a meta game together of trying together to take the story into interesting and weird places.

Again, good feedback!

comments.author: Cautious_Cry3928
comments.body: Cool concept, wondering if the same is possible with ComfyUI on your own server instead of relying on a DALL-E API. I think DALL-E probably has more reliable, less sloppy outputs than local diffusion models, but I can see the potential of buying a dedicated server with a GPU to do the same thing and dodge API costs.

replies.author: Philipp
replies.body:
Heya, good questions. So first of all, the reason I put it all up on Twitch was that this way, even if there's 10,000 users, it would cost the same in API costs. And those API costs are really negligible if the project was a success.

This would be different from, say, a locally installed app with a cloud API, which would then multiply in costs with every user. (A locally user-side LLM/ image generator would then of course fix that.)

With ChatGPT's new image generator, which was released after I programmed this last year -- but I already did speed tests now -- the main issue is that it's slower than the Dall-E API. Too slow for realtime use, but not by much. Once it would get fast enough, budget would be the next challenge, and for that challenge, a dedicated server with local models like you mention could come in handy.

ChatGPT's image generator does have great consistency, though (you can feed the API a reference image of your protagonist and such). And even greater prompt adherence than Dall-E.

The main problem right now though, I would think, are stickiness and finding users. It doesn't help that anything AI-related is practically banned in most of Reddit, and other places.

One thing we might look into is to use realtime video in the future. This might make the experience even stickier, especially if it feels like a living, breathing film world you move in. Fascinating!

replies.author: Cautious_Cry3928
replies.body:
Thanks for the response. It's a pretty cool project, and it has me thinking it would even make a great devops project to deploy to the cloud. (Working on IT certs right now and doing gamedev as a hobby)

Ya, X is the place for it. I'll give you a follow on Twitch and keep an eye out for it on X. Im sure this would go viral for a day or two if the right AI hype account tweeted about it. Don't be shy about promoting it there!
